title: sizer.f SWITCH=1/3: ts header misparsed as a data record -> blocks merge for non-round step numbers
description:
Same root cause as 6wo.20 but in the SWITCH=1 and SWITCH=3 loops, which still rely on the ts header accidentally parsing to cn=0 to terminate a block.

The header is written '(I15)' (wrt-csi.f:28, wrt-csi-fre.f:32-33). Read back with format 11/13 = (3X,I7),(3X,I7),... the second integer field lands on columns 14-15 of the header. So cn = the last two digits of the step number: it is 0 only when the step is a multiple of 100. For any other output interval the header parses as a bogus data record with cn!=0 and the block never ends -- consecutive timesteps are merged into one output row and atsum is the running sum across them.

Reproduced on REAL writer output (clu-fre, sample.3d, 200 steps, csi interval 20 => steps 0,20,...,200): sizer SWITCH=1 emits 3 rows instead of 11, with atsum 622/624/124 instead of ~125 each. Byte-identical pre and post 6wo.20, so 6wo.20 did not introduce or fix it.

Fix: apply the same shape as 6wo.20's SWITCH=2 loop -- terminate the record loop on LEN_TRIM(readln).le.15 (header) or EOF, before parsing, instead of on cn==0. SWITCH=1/3 writers never emit a cn=0 record (wrt-csi.f:30 and wrt-csi-fre.f:46,52 skip zero counts, loops start at i=1), so dropping the cn test is safe there.

Done criteria: SWITCH=1 and SWITCH=3 emit one row per timestep for a real-writer csi with a non-multiple-of-100 output interval; existing multi/sw3/cond/noterm/endterm/dangle/crlf fixtures still parse; -fcheck=all clean; smoke.sh baseline unchanged.

title: neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f: parallel neighbor list loses most neighbors under OMP_NUM_THREADS>1 (private local_counts/local_neighbors never merged across threads in SINGLE section)
description:
Reproduced with both the pre-9km and post-9km for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f (i.e. this
bug is entirely in neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f, unrelated to the force-loop file).

neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f's subroutine neighbor(step): local_neighbors(:,:) and
local_counts(:) are declared PRIVATE on the outer !$OMP PARALLEL construct, so
each thread gets its OWN copy, populated only for the atoms i it was assigned
by the DYNAMIC(32) schedule of the inner !$OMP DO. The merge step
(!$OMP SINGLE ... do i=1,natom ... local_counts(i) ...) then runs on exactly
ONE thread, reading ITS OWN private local_counts/local_neighbors — which only
has real data for the ~1/nthreads share of atoms that thread itself computed;
all other atoms' neighbor data (computed by the other threads) is silently
dropped (their private copies go out of scope, never merged into a shared
structure).

Effect: with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 the neighbor list is correct (single thread ==
single private copy == everything). With OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, atnlist ends up
with roughly 1/4 of the true neighbor count and is effectively wrong physics
for any run with >1 threads.

Repro: build apple-silent, run sample.3d (or any 3d file) with
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 vs OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and compare the neighbor-count column
in the "Step N: Updating neighborlist" screen output — count is stable (~194
for the shipped sample.3d) at 1 thread, and drops to a small, run-to-run
varying number (~45-90) at 4 threads.

Fix direction: merge each thread's local_neighbors/local_counts into the
shared atnlist inside the parallel region (e.g. an OMP CRITICAL/ORDERED
append per thread, or a two-pass count-then-fill using thread-local prefix
offsets) instead of relying on one thread's private arrays after the DO loop
ends.

title: sizer.f: EOF final-flush path is inconsistent with the per-block flush (all 3 switches)
description:
Two pre-existing quirks in the label-30 final-flush block of cluster/helpers/sizer.f, unchanged by w7w but now clearly visible:

1. Guard is 'ios.ne.0 .and. nts.gt.0 .and. .not.flushed'. A csi/fsi file containing exactly ONE timestep block produces ZERO output rows, because nts is only incremented by the per-block flush and the single block is flushed at EOF. Reproduced with b20/fsi_real1 (SWITCH=2, pre==post==0 rows) and, post-w7w, with the single-block fixtures cond.csi/sw3.csi. Likely the guard should be nts.ge.0 (or the nts counter bumped before the write).

2. The final-flush write omits the 'eks = eks - oek*ocn*ocg' subtraction that every per-block flush performs, so the last row's temperature column (col 5) is computed on a different quantity than all preceding rows. Visible in the w7w A/B: real_sw1.csi rows ts=120..180 (all-monomer blocks) give col5 = 0.00, but the identically-shaped last block ts=200 gives 150.56.

Affects SWITCH=1, 2 and 3 equally. Decide intended semantics before changing -- downstream pn/plot consumers may depend on current output.

title: sizer.f final EOF flush (label 30): missing ocg==atsum guard (div-by-zero) and nts>0 guard drops single-timestep files
description:
cluster/helpers/sizer.f lines ~254-257, shared by all three SWITCH paths:

  if (ios.ne.0 .and. nts.gt.0 .and. .not.flushed) then
    write (2,10) ts,ocg,otc,atsum-ocg, eks/((atsum-ocg)*1.5d0*cikb), ...

Two defects, both pre-existing and both fixed by the same edit:

1. No ocg.eq.atsum branch. The in-loop flushes (lines 103-108, 167-176, 227-232) guard this and write 0.0 for the temperature column when atsum==ocg; the EOF flush does not, so a final timestep whose largest cluster holds every atom divides by zero and prints Inf. Reproduced with the rvw2/fsi_zero fixture under SWITCH=2 post-6wo.20: last row column 5 = Inf.

2. nts.gt.0 suppresses the only output row of a single-timestep file. nts is incremented only by an in-loop flush, so a file with exactly one ts block (real case: clu-fre run shorter than 2 csi intervals) produces an empty output file with exit 0. Reproduced pre and post 6wo.20, all switches.

Fix: mirror the in-loop flush's ocg.eq.atsum branch and drop nts.gt.0 (keep real(cd)/nts safe by using max(nts,1) or by counting the final block before dividing).

Done criteria: single-block csi/fsi produces one row; a final all-in-one-cluster timestep prints 0.00 not Inf; existing fixtures unchanged apart from those two cases.
notes: Merged from a6r (duplicate, same sizer.f:247-250 flush block): three defects, one edit fixes all — (1) nts.gt.0 guard drops single-block files entirely (real single-block file yields 0 rows); (2) missing ocg.eq.atsum branch -> div-by-zero Inf in temp column; (3) final flush omits the eks=eks-oek*ocn*ocg subtraction, so last row's col5 uses a different quantity than per-block rows. Needs intended-semantics decision (downstream consumers may rely on current output). Also cosmetic while there: SW1 comment says records '47 or 63', SW3 says '47' — SW3 records are 53 chars; wrt-csi-fre guard is :46 not :45.

title: sizer.f writes integer literal 0 into REAL format field (F7.2) in ocg.eq.atsum branch at :98/:151/:200 — crashes with gfortran runtime type-mismatch error when a timestep is fully condensed into one cluster

Done: determine whether this is expected physics (box too small/hot for pbc+neighbor-pbc.o skin defaults) or a real neighbor-pbc.o bug, and fix or document; smoke.sh reports PASS for 'pbc'.

title: Harden omp neighbor builder: cap-overrun read, invalid SIMD, serial parity (dmmav, skin check)
description: Three pre-existing defects in cluster/neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f found in 3zk review, one pass fixes all: (1) P2 cap overrun — write side guards max_neighbors_per_atom=200 (line ~107) but merge read 'do j=1,local_counts(i)' (line ~123) iterates the UNCAPPED count: >200 neighbors reads past the atom's column into the next atom's slots (silently wrong indices; heap over-read for i=natom). Reachable: 5000 atoms in 8nm box hits 256-275. Fix: cap the merge loop AND add fatal stop on overflow like serial neighbor-pbc-mav.f list-full check. (2) !$OMP SIMD on the inner loop (line ~93) has loop-carried dependence via local_counts(i) increment — technically UB; remove directive. (3) Serial parity: omp version never assigns dmmav (prints 0.0) and lacks serial's skin-exceeded fatal check + adaptive atrskin update — port that logic from neighbor-pbc-mav.f. Done: dense 5000-atom/8nm run at 1 and 4 threads exits with clean physics or clean fatal (never silent corruption); dmmav printed nonzero matching serial semantics; 200-step sample byte-identity at 1 thread preserved.

title: Multi-thread statistical validation after omp fixes
description: Gate for trusting OMP_NUM_THREADS>1 end-to-end. Preconditions (wired as deps): 3zk neighbor merge fix, 6wo.4 epot mismatch resolution. Method: fixed-seed 200-step run 1 vs 4 threads byte-comparison of energies (expect near-identity per 9km review); plus ensemble check — 16 replicas single-thread vs 16 replicas 4-thread (different seeds), compare mean/std of final epot/T within statistical error. Deliverable: results in bead notes + PERFORMANCE.md section 'multi-thread validated: yes/no + caveats'. Done: verdict recorded; smoke.sh extended with a 2-thread sanity case if validation passes.

title: Campaign runner: N replicas across all cores
description: Deliverable: scripts/campaign.py (python3 stdlib only). Args: binary path, input .3d, -n replicas, --jobs (default: performance-core count via sysctl hw.perflevel0.logicalcpu), --seed-base. Each replica: own output dir runs/<name>/rep-NNN/, CLUSTER_SEED=seed-base+i, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 per replica (replicas saturate cores; no nested threading), manifest.json recording seeds/exit codes/durations. Failures reported, non-zero exit if any replica fails. Done: 8-replica run of clu-silent-omp on sample-derived input completes using ~8 cores (verify wall time ~1/8 of serial-sum), outputs + manifest present.
notes: Exit-code trap: until fortran-cluster-md skin-fatal bead fixed, a skin-exceeded fatal exits 0 — campaign runner should ALSO scan output for '*** FATAL' as failure signal, not exit code alone.

title: Deterministic seed control via CLUSTER_SEED env

title: Investigate: omp vs serial force epot mismatch at step 0 WITHOUT -ffast-math
description: From 9km review: with -ffast-math disabled, for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f disagrees with serial for-a-lj-n-pbc-m.f at step 0 (epot -3.38e-4 vs -2.29e-4 — ~50% relative, NOT FP noise); with full APPLE_FLAGS (incl -ffast-math) the two are byte-identical (verified in 8ok and 9km reviews). Suspicious: real expression difference that -ffast-math happens to compile identically, or reviewer's comparator setup differed (check neighbor object used, flags per binary). Reproduce carefully with identical flag sets before concluding. HEAD and post-9km omp agree exactly — predates 9km. Done: root cause identified in bead notes; if real divergence, fix + byte-identity re-check both with and without -ffast-math.
notes:
VERDICT: comparator artifact, not a real divergence. No code change made.

Reproduction: built two clu-silent-omp-equivalent binaries with IDENTICAL
flags/toolchain, differing ONLY in the force object linked
(for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.o vs for-a-lj-n-pbc-m.o), both linked against the SAME
neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.o (post-6wo.5). Deterministic input: cluster/sample.3d
copy with "pure random velocities after init" X->- (rndctrl; kps.f otherwise
seeds from wall clock) and 200 timesteps, screen-output every 10 steps.
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.

Flag set 1 (APPLE_FLAGS minus -ffast-math): -O3 -fopenmp -march=native
-funroll-loops -ftree-vectorize -std=legacy -ffixed-line-length-132
  -> outA.log vs outB.log: diff = EMPTY (full 200-step log byte-identical).
  Step-0 line in both: epot = -0.0002743303 (matches neither of the 9km
  numbers -3.38e-4 / -2.29e-4 — different run/config than whatever the 9km
  reviewer actually compared).

Flag set 2 (bare -O3, no -march/-ffast-math): -O3 -fopenmp -std=legacy
-ffixed-line-length-132
  -> also byte-identical full log.

Code inspection: for-a-lj-n-pbc-m.f and for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f are
term-identical in the force/energy math (same c1/c2/c3 constants, same
eps11/eps22/eps12, same per-pair fij/esum expressions, same accumulation
order per pair under OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 with STATIC schedule + REDUCTION).
The only textual differences are (a) omp computes `ij=api(i)+api(j)` before
the 1/rij2 inversion instead of after (order-independent, no effect), and
(b) `bf1=2.0d0+int(...)` vs `bf1=int(...)+2.0d0` (IEEE754 addition is
commutative bit-for-bit, no effect). Neither can produce a 50%-relative
epot mismatch; a real expression bug would show up here and it doesn't.

Conclusion: the 9km-reported mismatch (-3.38e-4 vs -2.29e-4 without
-ffast-math, byte-identical with it) was almost certainly a comparator
setup artifact -- most likely the two binaries compared were NOT built with
matching neighbor objects/flags (e.g. one still linked a stale/pre-6wo.5
neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.o, or a stale for-a-lj object left from a prior
toolchain build), not a real -ffast-math-masked expression divergence.
Given HEAD's omp force/neighbor pairing agrees byte-for-byte with serial in
every tested config (with and without -ffast-math, with and without
-march=native), no fix is needed.

Build artifacts and scratch run dir removed; `make clean` run; git status
clean (only pre-existing .beads/issues.jsonl diff, ignored per task).

title: stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f has same cvtnt/cvtn stack-overflow bug as -m.f (apple-frenkel latent crash)
description: stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f (used by apple-frenkel/FRENKEL/DIFFUSION/MOVIEFRENKEL targets) declares cvtnt(mxnlist),cvtn(mxnlist) (mxnlist=9e6, ~36MB each) as plain local arrays, same pattern fixed in stoddard-pbc-n-m.f by fortran-cluster-md-1kl. Under APPLE_FLAGS (-fopenmp implies -frecursive), these become ~72MB per-call stack frames, overflowing the default 8MB stack the first time stoddard() is called -> SIGILL/SIGSEGV at runtime (apple-frenkel currently still builds fine, this is a runtime-only latent bug, not caught by a build check). Fix: add 'save cvtnt,cvtii,cvtn,cvti,cvtl' (or equivalent) to stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f, same as the fix applied in stoddard-pbc-n-m.f. Verify with a short apple-frenkel run on sample.3d.
notes:
Scope widened per 1kl review: stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre-mov.f:30 has the SAME unsaved cvtnt(mxnlist) pattern — fix both -fre.f and -fre-mov.f (guard order also worth checking in both). Apply same fix as 1kl commit: save statement + verify arrays rebuilt-before-read.
vy6.3 smoke.sh testing found the frenkel and diffusion targets (both link stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.o, same missing-save cvtnt/cvtn pattern) ALSO crash with SIGBUS at the first 'call stoddard(-1)' in main.f under DEFAULT flags (no -fopenmp, no -frecursive) -- not just apple-frenkel as originally scoped. Reproducible every run (3/3) with the tiny 50-step smoke input. moviefrenkel (stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre-mov.o, same unsaved-array pattern per this bead's own notes) did NOT crash in the same smoke run -- inconsistent, possibly heap-layout luck rather than a real difference. Scope of the fix (save cvtnt,cvtii,cvtn,cvti,cvtl in stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f and -fre-mov.f) should be treated as blocking for frenkel/diffusion too, not just apple-frenkel. See fortran-cluster-md-vy6.3 smoke.sh run logs.

title: omp force routine computes different physics than serial sibling
description: Pre-existing divergence found in b3v review: cluster/for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f vs for-a-lj-n-pbc-m.f differ numerically, not just in parallelization: eps11=apeps(1)*apeps(1) vs apeps(1); eps12=apeps(1)*apeps(2) vs dsqrt(...); pair-type index ij=api(i)*10+api(j) vs api(i)+api(j); fij for 22/12 cases uses c222*eps22*12.0d0 with missing -c223 attractive term. The omp and serial binaries compute different forces/energies. Decide intended physics (serial sibling is the proven reference), align omp file to it. Done: side-by-side diff of the physics expressions shows equivalence; a short two-binary run on sample.3d produces matching energies within float tolerance.

Summary: 4 identical twins (atomc, boxpp, dmmpp, timep) + 1 identical-but-unused twin (connp), 5 divergent twins (atomp, const, cvtpp, energ, filep) - of which energ.inc divergence is moot (dead, unused by any helper). The remaining divergences (atomp, const/mxa, cvtpp, filep) all track the same root cause: helpers/ is a frozen 2004/2005-era snapshot predating cluster/'s later features (Nose-Hoover thermostat Q/psi/s/H, Frenkel-cluster tracking, carrier-gas counting, first-passage-time stats, cluster-size abort control). INCLUDE-RESOLUTION FINDING (empirical): gfortran quoted `include 'x.inc'` when compiling `-c helpers/foo.f` from cwd=cluster/ resolves ONLY relative to the source file's own directory (helpers/), NOT the invocation cwd (cluster/) and NOT any -I path (FLAGS has no -I). Two identical-but-dead twins (connp.inc, dmmpp.inc) could theoretically be deleted from helpers/ with zero effect (unused), but doing so still requires touching Makefile prerequisite lists for correctness/hygiene and provides no bug-fix value - left in place as out of scope for this audit-only bead.

notes: Done-criterion deviation, orchestrator-adjudicated: byte-identity at 1 thread holds for out.log/.csi/.ave but test.rst differs O(1e-14) (595 doubles, max rel 1.19e-14) — -ffast-math FMA-contracts the non-ATOMIC serial branch vs the ATOMIC parallel path. Arithmetic proven term-identical (mechanical branch-body diff); serial branch fully deterministic (t1==t4==rerun byte-for-byte, better than pre-change which differed t1 vs t4). Enforcing bit-identity would need -ffp-contract=off, negating the speedup. Threshold NATOM_PAR_THRESHOLD=2500; guard benefit re-measured: ~1.36x at 1 thread natom=1000-dense, ~parity at 4 threads.

title: Investigate: stoddard neighbor walk truncates at first non-type-1 neighbor
description: Found in 1kl review, pre-existing: cluster/stoddard-pbc-n-m.f — 'if (api(j).ne.1) goto 110' where label 110 is the LOOP EXIT, so the walk stops at the first non-type-1 neighbor instead of skipping it. In mixed-species runs (sample.3d has Ar+He) cluster detection may silently ignore neighbors after the first He. Possibly intentional (cluster analysis over species 1 only?) — check siblings stoddard-pbc-n.f / -fre.f for same pattern and thesis context in docs. Deliverable: analysis note in bead + fix if clearly a bug; if intent ambiguous, flag with bd human for operator physics decision. Done: bead notes state verdict with code evidence; any fix keeps 200-step energies identical for pure-species runs.
notes:
VERDICT: CLEARLY INTENTIONAL. No code change.

CONTROL FLOW (cluster/stoddard-pbc-n-m.f):
- Outer loop: do i=1,natom (line 77) ... enddo (line 109). Label 110 (line 108) sits directly before 'enddo' - it is the bottom of the OUTER i-loop body, i.e. 'go process next i', not a hard exit from the subroutine.
- Inner walk: for a given i, k=atnidx(i) (86); label 100 (88) is 'k=k+1; j=atnlist(k)' (advance to next neighbor entry); label 110 aborts the *entire remaining neighbor walk for atom i* and falls through to the next i.
- Line 82: if (api(i).ne.1) goto 110 -> atom i itself is skipped entirely unless it is species 1 (this is NOT in question, only the inner check was flagged).
- Line 91: if (j.lt.0) goto 110 -> normal end-of-list sentinel.
- Line 92: if (api(j).ne.1) goto 110 -> as soon as neighbor j is not species 1, the WHOLE rest of atom i's neighbor list is abandoned (not just j). A 'skip and continue' would instead be 'goto 100'.

WHY goto 110 == goto 100 HERE (no behavioral difference):
1. Neighbor-list build order is strictly ascending atom index for every builder wired to this routine: neighbor-pbc.f:75 'do j=i+1,natom', neighbor-pbc-mav.f:80 same, neighbor-pbc-mav-omp.f:98 same (OMP: inner j-loop still ascends per i, local_neighbors(j,i) appended in that order, merged in order at line ~131-141) - so atnlist(k) for a fixed i is monotonically increasing in atom index.
2. Species layout is contiguous with species 1 occupying the LOWEST indices, for the life of the run: read-3d.f:227-257 assigns api(j)=i for j=natom..natom+apnum(i)-1 in file order, and species index 1 (first block in the .3d file, e.g. Ar in sample.3d) is read first -> species-1 atoms always occupy indices [1, apnum(1)], every other species occupies higher indices.
3. Given (1)+(2): for atom i (species 1, since line 82 already filtered), its neighbor list j-values are ascending; once j crosses the species-1/non-species-1 index boundary, EVERY subsequent j is also non-species-1. So 'abort remaining walk' (goto 110) and 'skip this neighbor, keep scanning' (goto 100) visit the exact same set of species-1 neighbors and produce byte-identical cvtnt/cvtl - goto 110 is just an eager short-circuit exploiting the sortedness, not a different algorithm.
4. This invariant is NOT broken by mid-run atom-count changes: cluster/chg-natom.f (the only code that changes natom at runtime) is gated by chgNctl ('X'/'-' equivalenced to apNch(1), read-3d.f:239, atomp.inc:25) and the only shipped input cluster/sample.3d sets 'Change number: -' for both species, so main.f:152-153 never calls chgNatom() in the tested/shipped configuration. (Filed fortran-cluster-md-cjk as separate discovered-work: chg-natom.f itself never updates api() on insert/remove, which WOULD violate the contiguity invariant if that dormant feature were ever enabled - out of scope for this bead.)

INTENT EVIDENCE (species-1-only IS the design, not an accident):
- docs/CODE_MAP.md: cluster/cvtpp.inc table documents 'cgs(mxa), cgsf(0:mxa) | Carrier gas atoms per cluster' - the codebase's own vocabulary treats non-species-1 atoms as inert 'carrier gas', consistent with excluding them from the species-1 cluster network in this (earlier) routine.
- Sibling stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f (later variant, same author, 'thesis' progression) has the IDENTICAL two lines PRESENT BUT COMMENTED OUT: line 96 '*	  if (api(i).ne.1) goto 110' and line 105 '*	  if (api(j).ne.1) goto 110'. The walk there is deliberately generalized to include ALL species in the neighbor network, with species differentiation moved downstream into the cluster-statistics phase (cgs(cnum)/cgsf(cnumf) counters for non-species-1 members, lines 156-232) - i.e. the author explicitly evolved away from this restriction in the next-generation routine, leaving the disabled lines as a visible trace of the earlier design.
- stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre-mov.f (most recent variant) has NO trace of the api(i)/api(j) restriction in the walk at all - fully removed, same downstream cgs/cgsf pattern as -fre.f.
- stoddard-pbc-n.f, stoddard-pbc.f, stoddard-pbcsw-n.f, stoddard.f, stoddard-dummy.f: no api() usage whatsoever (single-species-only routines, multi-species question doesn't apply).

SIBLING TABLE:
| file | api(i)/api(j) restriction in walk | pattern |
|---|---|---|
| stoddard-pbc-n-m.f | active (lines 82, 92) | exit-at-first (goto 110) - proven equivalent to skip, see above |
| stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre.f | present but commented out (lines 96, 105) | disabled; superseded by downstream cgs/cgsf species split |
| stoddard-pbc-n-m-fre-mov.f | absent entirely | removed; same downstream split as -fre.f |
| stoddard-pbc-n.f / stoddard-pbc.f / stoddard-pbcsw-n.f / stoddard.f / stoddard-dummy.f | n/a | single-species, no api() |

CONCLUSION: stoddard-pbc-n-m.f's goto-110-on-non-species-1-neighbor is a correct, intentional optimization consistent with this routine's documented species-1-only cluster-network design; it produces identical results to a skip-and-continue given the neighbor-list ordering and species-contiguity invariants that hold throughout the current codebase. No fix applied. Discovered follow-up filed as fortran-cluster-md-cjk (chg-natom.f api()-tracking gap, dormant/unused in shipped inputs).

title: Toolchain-separated object files or clean between apple/ifort builds
description: From b3v review: apple targets and ifort targets write .o files to the same paths. make benchmark (builds apple-silent + silent) or any apple-then-ifort sequence without make clean silently links wrong-compiler objects. Options: per-toolchain obj subdir, or .o suffix per toolchain, or make benchmark insert make clean between the two. Done: make benchmark produces both binaries correctly from scratch; sequential apple-silent then silent build does not reuse stale objects (verify via file timestamps or nm).
notes: Additional scope from 8ok review: make clean only rm -f *.o — linked binaries (clu-silent-omp, clu-fre-omp, cluster, clu-*) survive; extend clean to remove them.

title: Re-parallelize omp force loop + cleanup orphans
description: b3v removed invalid OMP directives from the packed-neighbor-list force loop in for-a-lj-n-pbc-m-omp.f, leaving it serial (directives were unbuildable under gfortran and semantically broken: shared cursor k, DO WHILE not worksharing-able). To regain parallel speedup: restructure traversal so iterations are independent (e.g. per-atom loop over a CSR-style index array built by neighbor routine) then reapply OMP DO with reduction on esum and atomic/reduction on fsum arrays. Also cleanup: 6 orphaned !$OMP ATOMIC in the now-serial loop (pure overhead), unused variable tid (line ~20). Depends on physics fix bead — align expressions first, then parallelize. Done: apple-silent builds, multi-thread run on sample.3d matches single-thread energies, measurable speedup over serial force loop.
